Amendment 1407
AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 12 OF THE REVISED ORDINANCES OF 
2008 RELATIVE TO THE CREATION OF AN HONORARY
STREET-NAME DESIGNATION PROGRAM
Be it ordained by the City Council of the City of Worcester as follows:
Chapter 12 of the Revised Ordinances of 2008 be and is hereby amended by deleting section 
11A in its entirety and inserting a new section 11A as follows:
§11A. Honorary Street-Name Designation
 (a) There is hereby established an honorary street-name designation program as further 
provided in this section 11A.
 (b) The honoree of an honorary street name designation (“Designation”) must be a past 
or current resident, or residents, of the City that made a demonstrable and significant 
positive impact on the community or contributed to the cultural, economic, educational, 
intellectual, political, or scientific vitality of the community or have made an extraordinary 
contribution in the service of humanity. Commercial and corporate recognition does not 
qualify.
 (c) A Designation should be proposed through a petition filed with the city councilor in 
whose district the Designation will be located. If a petition is filed with a councilor-at-large 
or the mayor, the district councilor shall be notified of the petition prior to submission. The 
petition shall state the name of the individual(s) intended to be honored and the series of 
blocks to receive the Designation. The petition shall be accompanied by a biography of, and 
the reason(s) for honoring, the individual or individuals and a map indicating the blocks for 
the Designation. A Designation shall not extend beyond two contiguous blocks and shall be 
applied to a single street.
 (d) When the City Council approves a Designation, the street shall retain its official name 
and its legal status. The Designation shall consist of two signs, each to be installed on an 
existing pole at either end of the section of street designated. The Designation signs shall 
only be installed by the Department of Public Works & Parks.
 (e) That special consideration be given to the district councilor of whichever district the 
honorary street name will exist, as well as the Mayor, when the honorary street signage is 
planned for installation. Further, that such an event for the unveiling of the honorary street 
be planned through said district councilor and the city council office staff. 
 (f) The Designation shall be for a term of ten (10) years. If no new petition is pending for 
the same location, the Designation shall automatically renew for another ten years, unless 
otherwise voted by the City Council. Those streets which have been designated prior to the 
effective date of this ordinance shall be deemed to have been designated on the effective date 
of this ordinance and the first ten-year period shall commence on that date.

heading: Revised Ordinances of2008 Part One
text:
181
 (g) Upon adoption of such petition, a payment to the City in the amount established by 
the commissioner of public works and parks based on the actual cost to create the signage.
 (h) Additional requirements and restrictions.
(1) If a Designation proposal is considered and rejected, no new Designation 
proposal on behalf of the same individual or group may be requested for a period of 
one (1) year.
(2) When a section of street has received a Designation, no other proposals for that 
section of street shall be approved while it has that Designation.
(3) Proposals shall not be for names that could be considered derogatory, pejorative, 
or obscene.
4) The proposed Designation may not duplicate an official street name.
5) Only City of Worcester public streets are eligible to host a Designation.
 (i) At any time, the City Council may revoke and remove a Designation by a majority 
vote.

ADDRESSING SYSTEM FOR THE NUMBERING OF PROPERTIES AND

Be it Ordained by the City Council of the City of Worcester, as follows:
Section 1. Section Nine, Chapter Twelve of the Revised Ordinances of 2008, Part 
One, is hereby amended by deleting the existing section nine and inserting a new 
section nine as follows:
Chapter 12 – Streets and Sidewalks
§ 9. Address Numbers
(a) Purpose and Intent. The city finds that it is necessary and beneficial for the 
health, safety and welfare of the city to establish laws to provide for a standardized 
assignment of address numbers for properties within the city’s boundaries. The 
benefits of such a standardized addressing system include providing first responders 
with predictable addresses, facilitating the delivery of mail, goods and services, and 
increasing consistency and transparency.
(b) Standardized Addressing System. The chief development officer shall have the 
authority to establish, implement, and administer a standardized addressing system. 
Said authority shall include assigning address numbers to existing properties, to 
newly identified properties, and portions of properties. The chief development officer 
will notify the property owner whenever an address is assigned. The chief 
development officer is authorized to establish rules and regulations to further the 
purpose and intent set forth herein. The chief development officer shall maintain the 
Municipal Address Repository which shall contain all addresses assigned to 
properties in the city.
(c) Display of Assigned Number. The owner, agent or person having control of the 
property, or portion thereof, shall affix to the applicable property the number 
assigned, shall not affix or permit to remain on said property any number contrary to 
the direction of the chief development officer, and shall otherwise comply with the 
applicable rules and regulations. The authority granted under this ordinance shall be 
in addition to that granted by G.L. c. 148, sec. 59.
Section 2. Chapter Fifteen of the Revised Ordinances of 2008, Part One, is hereby 
amended by inserting a new subsection (J) immediately following subsection (I), to 
section 2(b)(8) Streets and Sidewalks, as follows:

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER THIRTEEN OF THE REVISED ORDINANCES 
OF 2008 RELATIVE TO MUNICIPAL PARKING FACILITIES AND THE USE OF 
ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS
Be It Ordained by the City Council of the City of Worcester, as follows:
Section 1. Chapter Thirteen of the Revised Ordinances of 2008, Part One, is hereby amended by 
inserting the following definitions in section 1:
electric vehicle – a battery electric vehicle that draws propulsion energy solely from an on-board 
electrical energy storage device during operation that is charged from an external source of 
electricity or a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle with an onboard electrical energy storage device 
that can be recharged from an external source of electricity which also has the capability to 
run on another fuel.
electric vehicle charging station – an electric component assembly or cluster of component 
assemblies designed specifically to charge batteries within electric vehicles by permitting the 
transfer of electric energy to a battery or other storage device in an electric vehicle.
Section 2. Chapter Thirteen of the Revised Ordinances of 2008, Part One, is hereby amended by 
deleting the definition of “vehicle” in section 1 thereof and inserting the following updated definition 
in lieu thereof:
vehicle - every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported, or 
drawn upon a street or highway, including bicycles and electric vehicles when the provisions 
of these ordinances are applicable to them.
Section 3. Chapter Thirteen of the Revised Ordinances of 2008, Part One, is hereby amended by 
inserting a new section thirty-seven A as follows:
§ 37A. Parking in Electric Vehicle Spaces Prohibited
(1) When official signs are erected giving notice thereof, no person shall stop, stand or park any 
vehicle, other than an electric vehicle, within either on-street or off-street municipal parking facilities 
specifically designated for the use of electric vehicle charging stations. These designated locations are 
reserved exclusively for electric vehicles that are actively charging at the station. Parking at an electric 
vehicle charging station without connecting to the charging station or remaining connected after the 
vehicle is fully charged is prohibited.
(2) Pursuant to this section, the Department of Transportation and Mobility and the Department of 
Public Works shall have the authority to designate municipal parking facilities for the use of electrical 
vehicle charging stations and to promulgate any rules and regulations related thereto.
Section 4. Chapter Thirteen of the Revised Ordinances of 2008, Part One, is hereby amended by 
deleting subsection (i) in section 36 thereof and inserting the following new subsections (i) and (j) in 
lieu thereof:
(i) A fine of forty dollars shall be imposed for each violation of § 37A.
(j) Every fine imposed in this section shall be increased by five dollars if not paid within 21 days 
from the date of issuance. Thereafter, upon notice by the parking administrator to the Registrar of
